I ran out of tool calls before packaging, so Phase 6 is not delivered yet. The code is written in my workspace, but there’s no tar.gz, the README isn’t updated, and I haven’t done the unused-resource sweep. Say “continue” and I’ll finish those and hand over the archive.

What Phase 6 does:

Trails, Measures, Directions and Time zones screens are now Jetpack Compose instead of fragments and RecyclerView adapters.
Data loading: the four screens update automatically from the database. The direction, measure and trail databases now each stay open once for the app’s lifetime instead of being reopened and closed on every action.
Shared parts: the list screens share one layout, one confirm dialog and one name-and-note dialog. The saved-locations screen now uses the same confirm dialog.
Trail names: one rule now checks new trail names in both places they can be created. A name can’t be blank, can’t contain / or \, can’t be the reserved database name, and can’t duplicate an existing trail (ignoring case).
New unit tests: TimeZoneCatalogTest and TrailNamesTest.
Behaviour changes you should know about:

Picking a time zone now closes the picker. The search text is no longer remembered between visits.
Trails and measures have a delete button, with a confirm step, instead of the old popup menu.
An empty trail note is saved as empty, not “N/A”.
“Navigate” tries Google Maps first and falls back to any map app.
Saving a direction no longer also sets it as the current target; you choose “Set” for that.
Files to delete (planned; I’ll confirm this after the unused-resource sweep):

Risks:

Not compiled. There’s no Android SDK in my sandbox, so nothing has been built. CI will be the first real check.
Saved directions could be lost. I rewrote DirectionModel from Java to Kotlin and kept the same table columns. If the table definition Room generates isn’t identical to before, Room will wipe the directions table on upgrade and saved directions would be lost. Check the CI build’s Room schema output for the directions database before installing on your phone. If it differs, tell me and I’ll keep the Java version, stripped down instead.
